title: The longest sign run of Keiper-Li second differences: a torus problem and its dual
description: Let cn = λn+1 − 2λn + λn−1 be the second differences of the Li coefficients. Assuming the Riemann hypothesis, every run of one sign of cn has length at most 593, improving the bound 621 of a previous paper. The companion torus problem, with free phases in the zero formula, has value between 589 and 593; under an independence hypothesis on the zero angles it equals the longest run of cn, and runs of 589 values of each sign occur with positive lower density. A duality theorem shows that a finite certificate exists exactly above the torus value. The constants are certified in ball arithmetic and the code is public.
